sections.heading: Objective 1: Autonomous Customer Service Agent
bullets: Building on last period's move from draft text to concrete proposed actions, we broadened what the agent can do end-to-end, including issuing and revoking individual discount codes, executing size swaps on pre-orders instead of merely offering them, and merging split shipments into one box, while extending the safety layer that freezes unshipped orders before any change is applied.

We rebuilt the agent's knowledge base by mining past resolved conversations into a curated set of articles with a weekly refresh loop, and gave the agent a search tool over it, so answers on sizing, shipping, and returns are grounded in verified facts rather than the model's own recall.

We ran a controlled head-to-head experiment comparing a newer, more capable AI model against our current one on accuracy, speed, and cost, and rejected it because it failed all three acceptance criteria, keeping our production model in place.

We added a triage pass that drops facts the agent can look up itself and auto-accepts tool-verified facts before founder review, and folded the founder's edits back into the agent's behaviour through a standing review-sheet feedback loop.

sections.heading: Objective 1: Platform Reliability and Correctness
bullets: We continued hardening the system against provider instability, adding automatic retries when reads from the helpdesk fail transiently, so drafts are not lost to momentary outages.

We fixed a set of intake failures where customer emails, replies arriving as new tickets, and attachment-only messages were being dropped or misclassified, so more incoming conversations reach the agent intact.

We closed a batch of security and data-integrity issues (a webhook authentication bypass, a secret leak, and corrupted finance snapshots) found during a code review, improving the platform's production readiness.

sections.heading: Objective 2: Partner Channel Discovery and Onboarding
bullets: Building on last period's outreach engine, we brought the partner conversation workspace to parity with our customer-service view, letting the operator draft, edit, send, pause, snooze, and reopen partner threads from one panel with saved-as-you-type composing.

We taught the discovery system to find prior history the engine had never looked for by searching past email threads, which surfaced additional live partner relationships, and we correlated incoming replies by sender domain so responses match the right company.

We built onboarding automation that generates a partner agreement, attaches it, and books an onboarding call from within the panel, moving toward the automated account-setup pipeline the objective requires.
The outreach engine remains hard-gated off by default pending quality validation, so no autonomous messages send yet.

sections.heading: Objective 3: Growth Intelligence
bullets: We continued extending our data ingestion beyond the customer-service and marketing feeds built last period, adding an expense-capture flow that reads receipts from a photograph and a corrected finance ledger, broadening the sources available for cross-source synthesis.

We built donation-routing intelligence that balances box allocations across partners by trailing-90-day volume and routes to a customer's own city first, an early autonomous decision layer over live partner data.
The unified synthesis and anomaly-detection layer needed to surface growth experiments remains ahead of us, with this period focused on widening the underlying data foundation.
